sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports lab functions
sections.what: Brings in the functions that list, look up and store golden moments.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests use the same functions the app uses, so they test real behaviour.
sections.watch_out: The lock tests use the same golden moments data, so changes here affect both files.

sections.name: lab moments before lock
sections.title: Checks moments are safe to show and sorted
sections.what: Checks there are 50 moments sorted with the highest leverage first. Checks the public list does not contain answer fields such as the reveal, winner, or match details. Checks each moment has at least two options and a valid overs format, that lookups by id work, and that the server keeps the full record.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fan must not see the answer before committing a pick, and the server needs the full record to grade it.
sections.watch_out: The answer-field check looks for exact key names in the data. A new answer field with a different name would not be caught.

summary: Tests the lab moment list: 50 golden moments sorted by leverage, and no answer hints in what a fan can see before locking.
purpose: Protects against revealing the outcome of a moment before a fan has committed a pick.
why: Likely reason: showing the answer before locking would make the fan game meaningless. Reason not stated in the code for the sorting order.
how: Lists the golden moments and checks there are 50, sorted with the highest leverage first. For each one, checks the JSON it produces does not contain answer-related keys, has at least two options, and has a valid overs format. Checks lookups by id return the right moment or nothing, and that the server still holds the full record.
inputs: The golden moments data stored with the app.
outputs: Pass or fail results. No files or database are changed.
risks: The banned-key check looks for exact quoted key names. A renamed field could leak an answer under a new name that is not in the list.
debug: If the banned-key check fails, find the key it names in the moment data and remove it from the public view. Check the sort order if the list looks out of order.
